> **What this case shows** — the previous case added the **Renyi** entropy, the *additive*
> generalization of Shannon. The **Tsallis entropy** is the other canonical one: *non-additive*,
> straight out of non-extensive statistical mechanics. This case introduces a **newly-authored op**,
> `tsallisEntropy`, completing the pair. On a real eyes-closed EEG channel it reproduces
> `NeuroKit2.entropy_tsallis` **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| ~**9e-16**) across **q = {0.5, 1, 2, 3}**.
> The punchline is *where the two families meet*: at **q = 1** the Tsallis entropy exactly recovers
> **Shannon** (2.325 nats) **and coincides with Renyi** — but at **q = 2** Tsallis (**0.885**) parts
> sharply from Renyi (**2.167**). Two roads through the same point.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for the non-additive entropy: `tsallisEntropy(x, q, bins)` → the order-q Tsallis entropy
of the signal's amplitude distribution (nats).
**Way of thinking** — "generalized entropy" is not one thing. Renyi keeps *additivity* and rescales;
Tsallis keeps a *power-law* form and gives up additivity. They agree only at q = 1 (both are Shannon);
pick the one whose axiom you want.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::tsallisEntropy()` (non-additive) alongside `renyiEntropy()` (additive);
both take `q`/`alpha = 1` to recover Shannon.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `tsallisEntropy` reproduces `NeuroKit2.entropy_tsallis` bit-for-bit (max
|diff| ~9e-16) across q = {0.5, 1, 2, 3}; at q = 1 it recovers Shannon (2.325 nats) and coincides with
Renyi, but at q = 2 it diverges from Renyi by 1.281 (0.885 vs 2.167); S_q is non-increasing in q.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a structural fact: the ecosystem had Shannon entropies and the additive
Renyi family — can we author the *non-additive* Tsallis family, reproduce the reference across q, and
show exactly where the two generalizations agree and where they part?** The goal is to introduce
`tsallisEntropy`, certify it bit-for-bit, and make the Renyi/Tsallis relationship concrete.

## Challenge & approach

Tsallis entropy is S_q = (1 − Σ p_i^q)/(q − 1), where p is the signal's amplitude histogram (the q → 1
limit is the Shannon entropy). We implement that closed form and check it against
`NeuroKit2.entropy_tsallis` on the identical histogram across a range of q — and, on the same axes,
overlay the Renyi entropy to expose the coincidence at q = 1 and the divergence elsewhere.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → tsallisEntropy(q, bins = 16) → S_q
                    vs NeuroKit2.entropy_tsallis (same histogram) → bit-exact (~9e-16) for every q
                    q=1 → Shannon (2.325) = Renyi;  q=2 → Tsallis 0.885 ≠ Renyi 2.167 (non-additive)
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the
[SVD-entropy](../svd-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd), [Petrosian](../petrosian-fd-eegmmidb/index.qmd) and
[Renyi](../renyi-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: two generalizations of Shannon as functions of their order — the Tsallis entropy S_q (red, op points; NeuroKit2 shown as black rings that sit exactly on them) and the Renyi entropy H_alpha (blue). The two curves cross at q = 1 (green point), where both equal the Shannon entropy; everywhere else they diverge — at q = 2 Tsallis is 0.885 while Renyi is 2.167 — because Tsallis is non-additive. Right: the POz amplitude histogram (16 bins), the distribution whose generalized entropy is computed.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel is the whole story — two families of generalized entropy that share
exactly one point (Shannon, at order 1) and part ways elsewhere; the op (red) sits on NeuroKit2 (rings)
at every q. The right panel is the distribution the entropy summarizes.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **Tsallis entropy, q = 1 (Shannon)** | **2.325 nats** |
| **Tsallis entropy, q = 2 (collision)** | **0.885 nats** |
| op vs `NeuroKit2.entropy_tsallis` (max \|diff\| over the family) | **9e-16** (bit-exact) |
| Tsallis vs Renyi at q = 1 (\|diff\|) | **0** (coincide — both Shannon) |
| Tsallis vs Renyi at q = 2 (\|diff\|) | **1.281** (diverge — non-additive vs additive) |
| non-increasing in q | **yes** |

The newly-authored op equals NeuroKit2 at every q, recovers Shannon at q = 1 (where it meets Renyi), and
diverges from Renyi elsewhere — the families' defining structure. Values trace to
[`artifacts/tsallis_summary.csv`](artifacts/tsallis_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`tsallisEntropy` completes the generalized-entropy pair — the ecosystem now has both the additive
(Renyi) and non-additive (Tsallis) families — and it is exact: bit-for-bit against NeuroKit2 across q,
with Shannon recovered at q = 1. The transferable takeaway: **"generalized entropy" is a fork, not a
single road. Renyi and Tsallis both pass through Shannon at order 1, but they answer different axioms
(additivity vs a power-law form) and give different numbers everywhere else — choose by the property you
need, not by habit.**

## Open questions

- The Tsallis index q, in non-extensive statistical mechanics, reflects long-range correlations /
  multifractality; estimating the q that best linearizes an EEG's generalized dimensions (a "q-triplet"
  analysis) and comparing it across brain states would turn the single fixed-q value into a
  physics-grounded descriptor. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Tsallis entropy (non-additive, order q) | `tsallisEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| Renyi entropy (additive, order α) | `renyiEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| SVD entropy / Petrosian FD | `svdEntropy()`, `petrosianFD()` | PhysioEEG |
| multi-measure complexity (Shannon-based) | `eegComplexity()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **q** — `1` is Shannon; `2` the (non-additive) collision-order entropy; larger q weights the most
  frequent amplitudes more strongly. Because S_q is non-additive, it is *not* interchangeable with the
  Renyi entropy of the same order — they agree only at q = 1.
- **bins** — the amplitude-histogram resolution (here 16); more bins resolve finer structure but need
  more data, and the absolute value is bin-dependent.
- **units** — nats (natural log), as in `NeuroKit2.entropy_tsallis`.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

tsallisEntropy(x, q = 2)   # non-additive collision-order entropy (nats)
tsallisEntropy(x, q = 1)   # = Shannon entropy (= renyiEntropy(x, alpha = 1))

# reproduces NeuroKit2.entropy_tsallis bit-for-bit across q (max |diff| ~9e-16);
# differs from renyiEntropy at every order except q = 1.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/tsallis_summary.csv`](artifacts/tsallis_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks
the collision and Shannon entropies, the bit-exact NeuroKit2 match over the q family, the coincidence
with Renyi at q = 1 and the divergence at q = 2, the monotonicity, and the honestly-noted scope
(newly-authored op; histogram-dependent; structure not absolute value).
